LESSON: WRITING 9.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: INSTRUCTION CHARTS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.3: Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing: Instruction charts

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing: Instruction charts. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should we give clear instructions?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. create instruction charts for information
2. appreciate the importance of clarity in written instructions

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 9.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: INSTRUCTION CHARTS
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing: Instruction charts helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 9.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: INSTRUCTION CHARTS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Create instruction charts for information

What this means
In this part you learn to create instruction charts for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create instruction charts for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing: Instruction charts”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create instruction charts for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the importance of clarity in written instructions

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of clarity in written instructions. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of clarity in written instructions.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing: Instruction charts to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of clarity in written instructions. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing: Instruction charts is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing: Instruction charts”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: create instruction charts for information)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing: Instruction charts to a partner. (skill: appreciate the importance of clarity in written instructions)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing: Instruction charts to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: create instruction charts for information.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the importance of clarity in written instructions.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing: Instruction charts from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing: Instruction charts: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing: Instruction charts?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we give clear instructions?
2. what went well and why?
3. what did not go well and why?
4. what can be done differently next time?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 9.3.1 Functional writing: Instruction charts means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: create instruction charts for information.
5. Be able to: appreciate the importance of clarity in written instructions.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
